claim: The Cyber Kill Chain is the attack model of Hutchins et al.
quote: The intrusion kill chain is deﬁned as reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control (C2), and actions on objectives.
issue: Hutchins names it the 'intrusion kill chain'; 'Cyber Kill Chain' is Lockheed Martin's later brand name for the same model, conventional and not a misreading. That the baseline attacker is modelled on it rests on brown2023 (not checked here); the six actions do not map one-to-one onto Hutchins' seven phases, and the sentence does not say they do.

claim: Hutchins et al. publish a lifecycle model of an attack with stages.
quote: this paper presents a new kill chain model, one speciﬁcally for intrusions.
issue: Seven phases, reconnaissance to actions on objectives, which map onto the four groups.

claim: Hutchins et al. describe an APT campaign whose intrusion attempt was detected and mitigated.
quote: a case study observed by the Lockheed Martin Computer Incident Response Team (LM-CIRT) in March 2009 of three intrusion attempts by an adversary is considered. Through analysis of the intrusion kill chains and robust indicator maturity, network defenders successfully detected and mitigated an intrusion
issue: APT framing: 'All three intrusions leveraged a common APT tactic' (same page).

claim: The campaign tried again the next day, with new recipients.
quote: One day later, another TME intrusion attempt was executed. Analysts would identify substantially similar characteristics and link this and the previous day’s attempt to a common campaign
issue: New recipients: 'the subject matter, recipient list, attachment name, and most importantly, the downstream IP address (216.abc.xyz.76) differed' (same page). 'Tried again after detection' is temporal; Hutchins does not say the adversary knew it was detected, and the sentence does not claim it.
